title: The Ertugrul Rescue and a Debt Repaid
text:
In September 1890 the Ottoman frigate Ertugrul was sailing home from a goodwill mission to Japan when a typhoon drove her onto the rocks off Oshima island, near Kushimoto in Wakayama. More than five hundred sailors died. The villagers of Oshima, poor fishing families, climbed down the cliffs in the storm to pull survivors from the sea. They carried them up, warmed them with their own bodies, and fed them their own scarce food, including their chickens. Sixty nine men survived, and Japanese warships carried them home to Istanbul.

In Turkey the story was taught in schools for generations. In Japan it was largely forgotten outside Kushimoto.

In March 1985, during the Iran-Iraq War, Saddam Hussein announced that after a 48 hour deadline any aircraft over Iran could be shot down. Foreign governments rushed to fly their citizens out of Tehran, but more than two hundred Japanese were stranded without seats. At Japan's request, Turkey sent Turkish Airlines planes, which flew the Japanese out shortly before the deadline. A Turkish diplomat later explained that Turkey had not forgotten the Ertugrul.
lesson: Kindness to strangers in distress is never wasted. It can be remembered and repaid by people you will never meet, long after you are gone.
people: Crew of the frigate Ertugrul, villagers of Oshima, Turkish Airlines crews
location: Kushimoto, Wakayama, Japan, and Tehran, Iran
source: Japanese and Turkish official accounts; contemporary press reports of the March 1985 evacuation from Tehran
